## How questions and the present tense work

Three patterns run through this whole chapter. Get these and most of the phrases below stop looking like random vocabulary.

1. **Question words go at the END.** Egyptian Arabic usually puts the question word *after* the rest of the sentence: **esmak eh?** is literally "your-name what?", and **enta feen?** is "you where?". This is the normal, neutral word order — not an emphatic one.

2. **The present tense takes a بـ (be-) prefix.** A plain present verb gets بـ in front to mean a habit or an ongoing action: **beteshta8al** = "you work / you're working", **bas7a** = "I wake up". You will see this prefix on almost every verb in this lesson.

3. **There is no verb "to have".** Egyptian uses عند (**3and**) plus a personal ending: **3andak** = "you have" (m.). The very same construction expresses age — **3andak kam sana?** is literally "you have how many years?".

Here are the core question words used below (إمتى is added for completeness):

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| إيه - eh | what |
| فين - feen | where |
| منين - meneen | from where |
| ليه - leeh | why |
| كام - kam | how much / how many |
| إزاي - ezzay | how |
| مين - meen | who |
| إمتى - emta | when |

## Examples

A few phrases that show the three patterns in action. Notice the question word landing at the end, and عند doing the work of "to have".

<details class="frase">
<summary>اسمك إيه؟</summary>
<span class="fr">esmak eh?</span>
<span class="en">What's your name? (lit. "your-name what?")</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إنت منين؟</summary>
<span class="fr">enta meneen?</span>
<span class="en">Where are you from? (question word at the end)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>عندك كام سنة؟</summary>
<span class="fr">3andak kam sana?</span>
<span class="en">How old are you? (lit. "you have how many years?")</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>بتشتغل فين؟</summary>
<span class="fr">beteshta8al feen?</span>
<span class="en">Where do you work? (بـ present + question word last)</span>
</details>

</details>

</details>

<span class="fr">banam el sa3a 3ashara kol yom</span>

</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>بشتغل من الساعة تلاتة لـ الساعة خمسة</summary>
<span class="fr">bashta8al men el sa3a talata le el sa3a 5amsa</span>

</details>

<span class="rotulo">Other useful expressions</span>

<details class="frase">
<summary>عندي فضول</summary>
<span class="fr">3andi fodool</span>
<span class="en">I'm curious</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>عندي كورس ألماني</summary>
<span class="fr">3andi course almani</span>
<span class="en">I have a German course</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>عندك شغل بكرة؟</summary>
<span class="fr">3andak sho8l bokra?</span>
<span class="en">Do you have work tomorrow?</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>نص نص</summary>
<span class="fr">nos nos</span>
<span class="en">So-so / half and half</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>العيش ده غالي</summary>
<span class="fr">el 3eesh da 8aali</span>
<span class="en">This bread is expensive</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>القهوة دي غالية</summary>
<span class="fr">el 2ahwa di 8alya</span>
<span class="en">This coffee is expensive</span>
</details>

The last two show the demonstratives **ده (da)** for masculine and **دي (di)** for feminine — "this". They come *after* the noun, and the noun gets the definite article: *el 3eesh **da*** = "this bread".

## Verbs in this lesson

All conjugated in the present (with the بـ prefix). The eight pronouns are أنا، إنت، إنتِ، هو، هي، إحنا، إنتو، هم.

**اشتغل - eshta8al — to work**

| Pronoun | Present |
|---|---|
| أنا - ana | باشتغل - bashta8al |
| إنت - enta | بتشتغل - beteshta8al |
| إنتِ - enti | بتشتغلي - beteshta8ali |
| هو - howwa | بيشتغل - beyeshta8al |
| هي - heyya | بتشتغل - beteshta8al |
| إحنا - e7na | بنشتغل - beneshta8al |
| إنتو - ento | بتشتغلوا - beteshta8alu |
| هم - homma | بيشتغلوا - beyeshta8alu |

**درس - daras — to study**

| Pronoun | Present |
|---|---|
| أنا - ana | بادرس - badris |
| إنت - enta | بتدرس - betedris |
| إنتِ - enti | بتدرسي - betedresi |
| هو - howwa | بيدرس - beyedris |
| هي - heyya | بتدرس - betedris |
| إحنا - e7na | بندرس - benedris |
| إنتو - ento | بتدرسوا - betedresu |
| هم - homma | بيدرسوا - beyedresu |

**اتكلم - etkallim — to speak / talk**

| Pronoun | Present |

| أنا - ana | باتكلم - batkallim |

| إحنا - e7na | بنتكلم - benetkallim |

**اتعلم - et3allim — to learn**

| Pronoun | Present |

| Pronoun | Present |

A small kit for building your own sentences: a few reference tables, some new verbs to try, and a couple of model sentences.

**Time and frequency adverbs**

| Arabic - franco | English |

| على طول - 3alatool | always |
| ساعات - sa3at | sometimes |
| كل يوم - kol yom | every day |
| مش... خالص - mesh... 5ales | never / not at all |
| أبداً - abadan | never |
| لسة - lessa | still / not yet |

| بكرة - bokra | tomorrow |
| إمبارح - embare7 | yesterday |
| قبل كده - 2abl keda | before that |
| دلوقتي - delwa2ti | now |

| بس - bas | but / only / enough |
| ولا - walla | or |

| من - men | from / since |
| لـ - le | to / until |
| مع - ma3 | with |
| من... لـ... - men... le... | from... to... |
| و - we | and |

| من غير - men 8er | without |

**Model sentences**

<details class="frase">
<summary>بصحى الساعة ستة وباروح الشغل</summary>
<span class="fr">bas7a el sa3a setta we baroo7 el sho8l</span>
<span class="en">I wake up at six and go to work</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>بتشتغل ولا بتدرس؟</summary>
<span class="fr">beteshta8al walla betedris?</span>
<span class="en">Do you work or study?</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>باتعلم عربي عشان عندي فضول</summary>
<span class="fr">bat3allim 3araby 3ashan 3andi fodool</span>
<span class="en">I'm learning Arabic because I'm curious</span>
</details>
